newsitem.title: NORWAY: Dyno to acquire 100 pct of Zambian venture.
newsitem.headline: Dyno to acquire 100 pct of Zambian venture.

text.p: Norwegian explosives and chemicals company Dyno Industrier ASA said on Tuesday it would acquire the remaining 70 percent of its Zambian joint venture Zambia Detonators Ltd (Zamdet).
The company said in a statement the acquisition represented a further step in Dyno's strategy for its global explosives business, Dyno Nobel, toward expanding its presence on the African continent.
The acquisition had been expected for months.
Zamdet is today jointly owned by Zambia Consolidated Copper Ltd (70 percent) and Nitro Nobel AB (30 percent), part of Dyno Nobel's European organisation, it said.
Zamdet, which began production of detonators in 1992, is in Chambishi, in the middle of the Zambian copper belt, and is managed by Dyno. It had a net turnover of over $7 million in 1996, Dyno said.
